items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: And so Fletcher came, and he had Roy and Chu in the band.

ctx.x: Well it was not really naughty. We’d become friends by that time. But John you know prided himself on everything, and was critical of Duke quite often. So then, and he had an ugly word or so to say about “Reminiscing in Tempo,” which Duke had written because his mother had died, and he was very serious at that time. And then John came out and heard the band and said, “What is that wonderful number?” We said, “John, we’re not going to let you forget that one.” And after that it was Fletcher Henderson who was…
